saints.name: St. Magnus of Füssen
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: The monk of St. Gall who carried the Gospel into the wild valleys of the Allgäu and founded the abbey of Füssen…
biography: Magnus (called Mang), a Benedictine associated with the monastery of St. Gall, laboured in the eighth century as a missionary among the people of the Allgäu in what is now southern Bavaria. He cleared forests, opened land, and is remembered as the "Apostle of the Allgäu."

He founded and served as abbot of the monastery of Füssen, where he died about the middle of the century. He became one of the most invoked local patrons of the region, called upon for the protection of crops and livestock against blight and vermin.
saints.knownFor: The evangelization of the Allgäu and the founding of Füssen abbey.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 6 September
